verse.text: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
verse.summary: Psalm 147 was likely sung after the exiles came home and Jerusalem's walls went back up — the verse just before this one says the LORD "gathereth together the outcasts of Israel." And the very next line says He counts the stars and calls them all by name. The God who runs the galaxies stoops to the most private wound you carry, and He doesn't just heal the broken heart — He binds it, like a careful physician wrapping what still hurts while it mends. Whatever has been broken in you for a long time, He has not forgotten it, and He is not finished with it.

sermon.title: Wilt Thou Be Made Whole?
sermon.excerpt: Thirty-eight years by the pool, and somebody always reached the water first. Jesus stood over his mat and asked a question that sounds almost rude — wilt thou be made whole? — then bypassed the water entirely: Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.

bibleStudy.title: Buy Your Own Oil

verses.text: Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom. And five of them were wise, and five were foolish. They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.

And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him. Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves. And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut. Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.

But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief. Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness. Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.

bibleStudy.excerpt: All ten virgins had lamps. All ten fell asleep. Only five had anything in reserve when the cry came at midnight — and nobody could lend the other five what they'd failed to buy in advance.
body: Start with the detail everybody skips because it ruins the tidy version of this story: all ten of them were virgins. All ten were invited. All ten had lamps, and all ten walked out to meet the bridegroom with what looked, from the outside, like identical faith. This was never a parable about five godly women and five scandalous ones. It's about ten people who showed up to church, so to speak — ten people doing the exact same religious activity, holding the exact same equipment, waiting on the exact same promise. The split in this story isn't between the people who believed and the people who didn't. It's between the people who believed and planned like it, and the people who believed and never got around to the planning part.

And here's the detail that should honestly make you laugh before it convicts you: "while the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept." Not the foolish five. All ten. Jesus did not write a parable where the wise virgins stayed up all night in intense prayer while the foolish ones partied and dozed off. Everybody fell asleep. The delay wore out the wise and the foolish in exactly the same way, because waiting on God is tiring for the real believers too — nobody gets a pass on fatigue just because their theology is sound. The difference between the two groups was never decided at midnight, in the panic, under pressure. It was decided earlier, quietly, before anybody was tired, in the boring unglamorous errand of filling a flask nobody was watching you fill.

Then comes the cry, and it comes at the worst possible hour for anybody caught unprepared: "at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh." No warning shot, no grace period, no gentle nudge an hour beforehand so the foolish five could scramble in time. Midnight — the hour nothing is open, nothing is convenient, nothing can be fixed quickly. "Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps," and that's the moment the foolish five finally discovered what they'd actually been carrying for all those hours: five lamps with nothing left to burn. Not empty on purpose. Not sabotaged by an enemy. Just never filled past what looked fine in the daylight, because a dry wick and a full one look exactly the same until you actually need the light.

So they do the only thing that makes sense to a person in a genuine emergency — they ask to borrow. "Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out." And the wise virgins say something that sounds cold on first read and is actually the most loving true thing anybody says in this entire parable: "Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves." That is not five selfish women hoarding supplies while their sisters go dark. That's five women telling the truth about a spiritual law the foolish five badly needed to hear a lot earlier: oil cannot be transferred at the door. Your mother's prayer life cannot be poured into your flask at midnight. Your pastor's anointing was never meant to cover for the devotion you skipped. Your spouse's faith, however strong, cannot be subdivided and handed to you in a crisis. Whatever relationship with God you actually have when everything is calm is the exact relationship you will be standing on when everything is not.

Watch what happens next, because this is the part of the story that should put the fear of God in you in the best possible sense: "while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut." The door was shut. Not locked for an hour. Not cracked for latecomers with a good excuse. Shut, final, while five virgins were still out running an errand they should have run weeks earlier. "Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not." Read that title again — Lord, Lord. These weren't strangers banging on a door they'd never approached. These were five women who had worn the same outfit, carried the same lamp, used the same vocabulary as the five who got in. And the Bridegroom's answer wasn't "you're a little late." It was "I know you not" — the single most terrifying sentence in the entire New Testament, because it isn't aimed at an obvious enemy. It's aimed at somebody who looked, right up until midnight, exactly like family.

Paul takes this same picture and turns it into instruction instead of warning, because the church at Thessalonica was asking the same question we ask — when is He coming back? — and Paul redirects the whole conversation: "But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief. Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day... Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober." Notice Paul doesn't tell them to stop sleeping — he already knows, same as Jesus' parable already told you, that everybody gets tired in the waiting. He tells them to be sober, which is a different instruction entirely. You can be asleep and still have oil in the flask. You cannot be sober and still be unprepared, because sober is a decision you keep making in the daylight hours, long before anyone sounds the midnight cry.

Here's my real question for you today, and I need you to actually sit in the discomfort of it instead of assuming it's for somebody else: is your relationship with God currently running on your own oil, or somebody else's? Maybe you grew up in church and the faith in the room has always just felt like ambient light — your grandmother prayed, your parents believed, the whole house ran on devotion you never personally had to produce. That's a beautiful inheritance and a dangerous substitute, because inherited light runs out exactly when you need it most, and nobody in that family line can lend you theirs at the door. Maybe it's not inheritance — maybe it's just momentum. You went through a season once where your walk with God was real and full and burning, and you've been quietly running on the memory of that season for longer than you'd like to admit. A memory is not oil. A testimony from five years ago will not light tonight's lamp.

So don't wait for the midnight cry to go shopping, because the parable is brutally clear about what happens to the people who do: they run the errand at exactly the wrong hour, and the door is shut while they're still out running it. Buy your own oil now, in the boring ordinary daylight, while the shops are open and nobody's watching and there's no applause for it. That means your own prayer, not just the prayers said over you. Your own time in the Word, not just the sermon you heard secondhand. Your own obedience, your own repentance, your own relationship with the Bridegroom that doesn't collapse the moment the people who've been carrying you get tired of carrying you. Nobody is coming to subdivide their walk with God and hand you a share of it in a crisis — go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves, today, while today is still called today.

So trim your lamp now, while it costs you nothing but a little discipline nobody's clapping for. Fill the flask before you're tired, not after. Let your light be your own, your oil be your own, your readiness be your own, so that whenever the cry comes — and it will come, at an hour none of us get to schedule — you're not out running an errand you should have finished long ago. You're already inside, the door already open, the Bridegroom already saying your name instead of the sentence that ends every excuse: I know you not. Watch, and be sober, and be found ready. In Jesus' name, amen.

lines: Father, I declare today that I will be made whole — I am done making peace with what You came to heal!
You saw me lying there, and You knew how long — not one year of my waiting was hidden from You!
The length of my wait does not set the length of my deliverance!
I have no man — but I have the Son of Man, and He does not need the water to move!
When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up!
No one will step down before me into what God has written for me!
I rise! I take up my bed! I walk!
What used to carry me, I now carry as a testimony!
He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds — and that includes mine!
Save this. Speak it over your house today. Rise, take up thy bed, and walk — I will be made whole! In Jesus' mighty name, amen!

dreamFire.title: The Key Is Not In Their Hand
dreamFire.intro: Tonight's shield prayer is not about any one locked door or hidden room — it meets every form of dream imprisonment: every cage, chain, pit, dungeon, and barred gate the enemy builds while you sleep. No matter what shape the trap takes, the keys were never his to keep. Pray this aloud before you close your eyes, in Jesus' name.
points: Father, Your Word declares in Isaiah 42:7, "To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house" — every cage built around me in the dream realm tonight is opened, every chamber of darkness is lit, and I am brought out free, in the mighty name of Jesus!

By the authority of Zechariah 9:11, "As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water" — every pit dug for me in a dream, every dry well with no way of escape, releases me now by the blood of the everlasting covenant, in Jesus' mighty name!

I stand on Psalm 107:16, "For he hath broken the gates of brass, and cut the bars of iron in sunder" — every brass gate shut against me in the dream realm is broken, every iron bar locking me into a dark room or chamber is cut in sunder tonight, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Father, as in Acts 5:19, "...the angel of the Lord by night opened the prison doors, and brought them forth..." — send Your angel to every prison built around me while I sleep tonight; let every locked door fly open by night, and let me walk out free before the sun rises, in Jesus' mighty name!

By the anointing in Isaiah 61:1, "...to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound" — I receive liberty over every captivity assigned to my sleep tonight; every prison of the night is opened, and I am loosed completely, in the mighty name of Jesus!

I decree by Psalm 146:7, "...The LORD looseth the prisoners" — whatever bound my hands, my feet, or my voice in a dream tonight is loosed now by the same God who looses every prisoner, in Jesus' mighty name!

Father, as in Lamentations 3:55-57, "I called upon thy name, O LORD, out of the low dungeon... Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry... Thou drewest near in the day that I called upon thee: thou saidst, Fear not" — from every low dungeon of the dream realm I call on Your name tonight, and I declare that You draw near and speak fear not over my life, in the mighty name of Jesus!

I stand on Psalm 68:6, "God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains..." — every chain fastened on me in a dream tonight, every attempt to isolate me from my family and my destiny, is broken, and I am brought out and set in place, in Jesus' mighty name!

By the Word in Zechariah 9:12, "Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee" — I am not a prisoner of darkness tonight, I am a prisoner of hope; I turn to the Stronghold, and I receive double for every night the enemy tried to hold me captive, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Father, Your Word declares in John 10:9, "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture" — I reject every false door, every strange gate, every counterfeit entrance opened to me in a dream; Jesus alone is my door, and through Him I go in and out in safety, in the mighty name of Jesus!

By the authority of Revelation 1:18, "I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death" — no spirit, no altar, no dream tribunal holds a key over my life; Jesus Christ alone holds the keys of hell and of death, and I am sealed in His hand, in the mighty name of Jesus!

I take authority from Matthew 16:19, "And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven" — I bind every power that tried to trap me in my sleep, and I loose myself from every cage, chain, and closed door assigned against me, in the mighty name of Jesus!

So I seal tonight with Isaiah 22:22, "And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open" — every door the enemy tried to shut on my destiny in the dream realm, He has opened, and no power can shut it again; every door he tried to open against me, He has shut, and none can open it. I will wake in the morning free, unchained, and unafraid — in the mighty, all-consuming name of Jesus Christ, amen! 🔥
